answer: Before any agent can trade, route it through Stripe Identity: the check matches a government ID against a live selfie, and Stripe keeps only a hash of the document, so one passport backs exactly one account. A forger pays $1.50 per check plus a fresh ID's black-market price, and after fifty duplicate hashes the batch is banned outright, like a sonnet collapsing when one line breaks the rhyme. Fake signups swarm like nectar draws bees on a terrace, yet duplicate hashes merge into one banned fingerprint, and the farm starves before its first trade clears.
